# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pārājika 4 (Bu-Vb Pj4)

**Title (English, from literature):** The training rule on falsely claiming a superhuman quality

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pārājika 4 (*Uttarimanussadhamma*) is the fourth rule of defeat (*pārājika*) in the Theravāda *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha* and its commentary in the *Vinaya Piṭaka*. The rule mandates expulsion from the saṅgha for any monk who falsely lays claim to a superhuman quality or profound spiritual attainment (*uttarimanussadhamma*), such as knowledge and vision (*ñāṇadassana*) or arhatship [Bechert 1992]. The Vibhaṅga defines the consequence of expulsion using the simile of a palm tree whose crown is cut off, unable ever to grow again (*seyyathāpi nāma tālo matthakacchinno abhabbo punavirūḷhiyā*) [Clarke 2009]. In the canonical origin story, monks spend the rains retreat on the banks of the Vaggumudā (or Valgumudā) river and praise one another's false spiritual attainments to householders to procure abundant alms; the Buddha sharply rebukes them, declaring that one who obtains support by lying about spiritual attainments is the greatest of thieves [Rosen 1959].

Scholars have noted that the Vinayavibhaṅga on Pārājika 4 interprets *ñāṇadassana* in a soteriological sense, encompassing the "three knowledges" (*tevijjā*) culminating in arhatship, rather than purely visionary experiences of divine beings [Bechert 1992]. The transgression is closely connected to the prohibition against intentional lying (*sampajānamusāvāda*), recalling *Pācittiya* 1 as well as *Pācittiya* 8, which penalizes announcing real superhuman attainments to the unordained [Rosen 1959; Collins 1993].

*Pārājika* 4 is paralleled across all extant Vinaya traditions—including the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, and Dharmaguptaka recensions of the Bhikkhu and Bhikkhunī *Pātimokkha* and *Vibhaṅga*. The origin story of the Vaggumudā monks is shared verbatim with Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga *Pācittiya* 8, a substantial textual reuse confirmed by DharmaNexus, which records 1,595 matches (178,998 characters) between the two texts [Rosen 1959; DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns substantial narrative and doctrinal segments with the *Lakkhaṇa Saṁyutta* (SN 19), the Chinese *Saṁyuktāgama* (T 99), and Tibetan Vinayavibhaṅga texts [DharmaNexus].
